schema.title: Response Health Api V1 Health Get

get.description:
Restart consent for the logged-in recruiter. Reuses the same state-binding
CSRF cookie as /google/login; the existing /google/callback + upsert_recruiter
already replace the stored tokens and flip account_state back to ACTIVE
(retaining the existing refresh token if Google omits a new one).

post.description:
No get_current_recruiter dependency, deliberately — logout must be
idempotent with no session (AC-02), not 401. Safe without CSRF protection
because the session cookie is SameSite=Lax: a cross-site POST doesn't carry
it, so an attacker can't trigger this against a logged-in victim.

put.description:
Replaces the full field set: the client sends the whole ordered array,
the server reconciles it against existing rows by `field_id` (keep/update
when present, insert when absent, delete when missing from the payload) —
this is not a partial update.

schema.title: Response Available Slots Api V1 Scheduling Available Slots Get

ApplySuccessOut.title: ApplySuccessOut
ApplySuccessOut.description:
No candidate_id: an internal UUID has no business reaching an
unauthenticated caller, same reasoning as PublicJobOut.

AvailableSlotOut.title: AvailableSlotOut
AvailableSlotOut.description: Computed and bounded by ?count=, never Page[T] (ADR-004 P5).

ProcessStatusOut.title: ProcessStatusOut
ProcessStatusOut.description:
total/processed/failed are computed over candidates.submission_status —
there are no such columns on any table.

PublicJobOut.title: PublicJobOut
PublicJobOut.description:
Exposes only what a candidate needs. No recruiter identity, no job id,
no counts — an unauthenticated caller has no business seeing any of that.

TemplateFieldIn.title: TemplateFieldIn
TemplateFieldIn.description:
`field_id` present = keep this existing field row; absent = create a new
one. Load-bearing: `candidate_form_responses.field_id` is an FK, so treating
every save as delete-and-recreate would cascade away submitted responses.
